theorem.statement: In the original A(1,1) Serre algebra, let gamma=(a,b,n) be a nonzero formal degree with a,b,n nonnegative, and put u=a-n, v=b-n. If at least one of |u|, |v| or |u-v| exceeds 1, then the ENTIRE formal root space g_gamma is zero. If (u,v)!=(0,0) and g_gamma is nonzero, then g_gamma has dimension one. The case u=v=0 is not determined by this theorem.
proof: For A(1,1) write h1(gamma)=2a-b-n, h2(gamma)=2b-a-n, h3(gamma)=2n-a-b. Their sum is zero. They all vanish exactly when gamma is a multiple of delta=(1,1,1). If gamma is not a delta multiple, at least one h_i(gamma) is positive.

A positive formal component supported at only one simple root has dimension one at the simple root and is zero at every larger multiple: the positive algebra is generated by e1,e2,e3 and a Lie word containing only copies of one generator vanishes beyond its first copy. For a non-simple positive root gamma with nonzero component, at least two coefficients are therefore positive.

Choose i with h_i(gamma)>0. The actual locally finite Chevalley exponential automorphism tau_i maps g_gamma isomorphically to g_(s_i gamma); s_i gamma is obtained by subtracting h_i(gamma) from the i-th coefficient. At least one other coefficient remains positive, so the image cannot be a wholly negative root. Mixed-sign components are zero by the actual positive/Levi/negative decomposition. Thus s_i gamma is another nonzero positive root and its integer height is strictly smaller. Every s_i fixes delta and is invertible, so a non-delta degree cannot become a delta multiple. Descending height must therefore terminate at a simple root, never at an unproved imaginary root. This establishes that every non-delta nonzero root component is isomorphic to a one-dimensional simple-root component.

Under s1, (u,v) becomes (v-u,v); under s2 it becomes (u,u-v); under s3 it becomes (-v,-u). In each case the three signed quantities u,v,u-v are permuted up to sign. For every simple root they all belong to {-1,0,1}. The property is therefore necessary for every non-delta root reached by reflection descent. If any of their absolute values exceeds 1, the original root component must be zero. No invariant form or rank computation is used.

degree_five_application: At r=s=1 and n=5, every actual entire formal source g_(a,b,5) vanishes whenever |a-5|>1 OR |b-5|>1 OR |a-b|>1. In particular this criterion applies to every original critical type whose literal (a,b,5) satisfies that uniform condition; it is stronger than merely saying its ordinary D3 kernel vanishes. For any such original type mu, Q1/Q2 then give M_mu(F_free/G)=M_mu((D(C) intersect J)/D(I))=0, and M_mu(T)=0 because T injects into the latter quotient with FULL denominator D(I) intersect Y. The condition is an analytic family, not an executed or selected numeric probe. It does not apply to delta degrees and makes no invariant-source claim. The separate adjoint theorem proves the degree-(4,4,5) source is one-dimensional and injective, not zero.
